title: Lesson 18 - Group Sharing Scenarios (Sharing Sets, Groups vs Teams)
description: Given a scenario, determine how groups and sharing sets support record access, and contrast groups with teams.

questions.question: Partner portal users must see the Opportunities belonging to their own Account. Which configuration is appropriate?
options: A public group with a sharing rule
A sharing set mapping the portal user's Account to Opportunity access
Setting Opportunity OWD to Public Read Only
questions.explanation: Sharing sets use the portal user's Account/Contact relationship to grant access to related records - exactly the B2B portal pattern. Public groups and account teams do not derive from the portal user's account, and relaxing OWD over-exposes.

questions.question: Which is the correct comparison between public groups and teams?
options: Teams are org-wide; groups are per-record
Groups are reusable targets for sharing rules across populations; teams grant per-record, owner-managed access
Teams cannot be enabled on Account
questions.explanation: Public groups are reusable, population-level targets for rules; teams are per-record, owner-configured grants. They solve different scale problems and are not interchangeable.

questions.question: An org needs every member of the East-Sales group to see all Accounts owned by the West-Sales group. What is the cleanest solution?
options: An Account Team for each account
A public group (East-Sales) and an ownership-based sharing rule sharing West-Sales-owned accounts to it
questions.explanation: Ownership-based sharing rule to the target group (East-Sales) is the population-level solution. Per-record teams do not scale, sharing sets are for external users, and queues are for assignment.
